newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat escapes worries with his adopted children.
newsitem.headline: Arafat escapes worries with his adopted children.

text.p: Yasser Arafat, the guerrilla leader turned statesman, on Saturday celebrated the Moslem feast of Eid al-Fitr by doing what he loves -- spending time with his adopted children.

Over the past two decades Arafat adopted 75 children from Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon whose parents were killed by the Syrians, the Israelis and their allies during the hot years of Arab-Israeli conflict in the Middle East.

Arafat and his wife Suha had their first child, a daughter named Zahwa, 18 months ago, but on the first day of the holiday that marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan, Arafat spent much of his time with his adopted children.

When Arafat arrived at the house where the children live in Palestinian self-ruled Gaza, the children ran to greet him, throwing themselves cheerfully at him. The house is located just a few miles away from Arafat's office along the Gaza coastline.
Arafat embraced and kissed the children, forgoing lunch to to help feed the children climbing and tugging at him.
"I forget my worries when I am with them, they are my children, I brought them up myself," Arafat, 67, told Reuters.

"President Arafat is a completely different person when he is with the kids. He sits on the floor to play with them, he listens to their problems and looks after them. He actually spoils them," a PLO official said.

Only 35 of the adopted children moved to Gaza from Tunis with Arafat in 1994 when he took control of parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip under a PLO-Israel peace deal. The 40 other children were either studying in Europe or had married.
Through the years Arafat has provided the orphans -- some infants at the time of their adoption -- with shelter, care and education. They reside in a house named the Steadfastness House.
Arafat says he finds refuge from daily pressures by spending time with his adopted children.
Radwan Radwan, the supervisor of the 'Steadfastness House' said: "Five of the children here in Gaza carry Yasser Arafat's name, three boys and two girls."
Three of Arafat's adopted daughters were recently married, one to a Gazan. Arafat danced at her wedding.
The orphans moved with Arafat to Tunis from Lebanon in 1982 after the PLO was ousted during the Israeli invasion of Lebanon. From Tunis he moved in 1994 to Gaza.
The children complained that they used to spend more time with Arafat when they resided in Tunis.

"Now we only see him on occasions such as the Eid and during Ramadan," said Lina Yasser Arafat, 15. "He is a very tender, loving and caring father. He plays with us and takes very good care of us. He is the only family I have."
